title: Zeta functions of quasi-split reductive algebraic groups over local fields
summary: We calculate zeta functions of quasi-split reductive algebraic groups over local fields using the classification of Tits and prove a functional equation. We give explicit exam- ples of these zeta functions for non-split unitary and orthogonal groups.

title: Geometrization of Kottwitz-Shelstad transfer and Vogan's conjecture on local Arthur packets
summary: We give a geometric analogue of Kottwitz-Shelstad transfer for a general class of reductive groups over p-adic fields with cyclic component groups of trivial or prime order. We prove that this geometric transfer coincides with Kottwitz-Shelstad transfer, adapted to the language of disconnected groups, assuming the local Langlands correspondence satisfying certain desiderata, including the Kazhdan-Lusztig hypothesis for the ambient group and its endoscopic groups. As an application of this geometrization, we prove Vogan's conjecture on local Arthur packets over p-adic fields: for quasisplit classical groups and their pure inner forms, all local Arthur packets are ABV-packets, and the distributions attached to these ABV-packets of Arthur type satisfy Arthur's local conjectures on twisted endoscopic character relations. This demonstrates the following general principle: for any reductive group G over a local field, an Arthur packet should be defined as an ABV-packet of Arthur type, equipped with the endoscopic pairing calculated by traces of actions on vanishing cycles or microlocalizations.

title: A resolution of the Steinberg module of a parabolic subgroup of GL_n
summary: Let F be a field, G = GL_n(F), and let St be the Steinberg module of G. For a parabolic subgroup P of G, let St_P be its Steinberg module. There is a natural map rho_P: St -> St_P corresponding to intersection of a modular symbol with the Borel--Serre boundary. We construct a ZP-resolution Sh_P of St_P, the P-sharbly resolution. We also construct a P-equivariant chain map from the sharbly resolution of St to the P-sharbly resolution of St_P which enables us to compute the map induced on Steinberg homologies by rho_P. In the case when F is a number field and Gamma subset G is a torsion-free arithmetic subgroup, rho_P induces the restriction map H^(Gamma, E) -> H^(Gamma cap P, E) via Borel--Serre duality, for any coefficient module E which is flat over the base ring. If E is a vector space over Z/pZ this provides a computation of the restriction map on cohomology from Gamma to Gamma cap P in terms of sharblies, which enables the study of this restriction map in characteristic p, where Eisenstein series cannot be used.

title: Hammock coordinates for silting subcategories of derived-discrete algebras
summary: We introduce hammock coordinates to study the combinatorial structure of partial silting configurations in the bounded derived category of a derived-discrete algebra $Λ(r,n,m)$. By extracting exact integer inequalities from the Bobiński--Geiß--Skowroński Hom-hammock formula, we establish a closed-form criterion for pairwise partial silting both within any $\mathcal Z$-component and across distinct components. Using this coordinate framework, we establish three primary results. First, we prove the universal upper bound $|S| \le n+m$ on the cardinality of any partial silting configuration $S$ of $\mathcal Z$-objects ---both globally via Bongartz completion in the silting-discrete setting, and combinatorially within a single component via a $Σ^r$-invariant staircase argument. Second, we prove that this bound is universally sharp by constructing an explicit L-shaped partial silting configuration of size $n+m$ for every $Λ(r,n,m)$, alongside specialized diagonal configurations. Third, we show that the configuration lattice carries a faithful action of the cyclic group $\mathbb Z/g$ where $g = \gcd(r+m, n-r)$. We conclude by showing a structural obstruction to local determination: pairwise partial silting of consecutive objects in the lattice ordering does not imply global partial silting, due to the strict additivity of a coordinate defect along chains.

title: Representations of Bound Quivers over $\mathbb{F}_1$ and Hall Algebras
summary: Representations of quivers over the virtual field $\mathbb{F}_1$ can be naturally extended to bound quivers with monomial and commutativity relations. In this paper, we introduce and study the Hall algebra $\mathcal{H}_{\mathbb{F}_1}(Q,I)$ for a bound quiver $(Q,I)$ equipped with such relations. As in the quiver setting, $\mathcal{H}_{\mathbb{F}_1}(Q,I)$ is a graded, connected, and cocommutative bialgebra, and the free subgroup generated by all indecomposable representations forms a Lie subalgebra. We study $\mathcal{H}_{\mathbb{F}_1}(Q,I)$ in detail for two special classes of bound quivers: Nakayama bound quivers and gentle one-cycle bound quivers. In both cases, we prove that for any triple $L, M, N$ of $\mathbb{F}_1$-representations over $(Q,I)$, the Hall number $g_{N,L}^M$ coincides with the evaluation of the corresponding Hall polynomial $φ_{N,L}^M(t)$ at $t=1$. Consequently, there exists a canonical isomorphism between $\mathcal{H}_{\mathbb{F}_1}(Q,I)$ and the degenerate Hall algebra $\mathcal{H}_1(Q,I)$, justifying Tits's $\mathbb{F}_1$-philosophy in these settings.

title: Correlators of the Jacobi Unitary Ensemble on a General Interval and Hurwitz Numbers
summary: We study correlators of the Jacobi Unitary Ensemble $\mathbf J(p,q,α,β,N)$ of Hermitian matrices with spectrum in an arbitrary real interval $[p,q]$. For $(p,q)=(0,1)$, Gisonni, Grava and Ruzza expressed the large-$N$ expansion of the correlators $\langle\prod_j \mathrm{tr}\,X^{λ_j}\rangle$ through triple monotone Hurwitz numbers. We extend this genus expansion to arbitrary $p,q$ with $α/N$ and $β/N$ fixed. Using the Frobenius characteristic map and the idempotent basis of the center of $\mathbb C[\mathfrak S_n]$, we also obtain an explicit formula for the Schur--Selberg type integral $\int_{(p,q)^N}χ_λ(x)\,Δ^2(x)\prod_a (q-x_a)^β(x_a-p)^α\,\mathrm{d}^Nx$ in terms of irreducible characters of the symmetric group and content products. As consequences, we describe the zero-mean ensemble, and we recover, term by term in the genus expansion, the polygon-gluing formula for the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble in the limit $c_A=c_B\to\infty$. Structurally, passing from $[0,1]$ to $[p,q]$ leaves the hypergeometric weight of the associated 2D Toda tau function unchanged and only changes the specialization of its second set of times.

title: Closed energy formulas on tensor squares of perfect crystals of types $D_4^{(3)}$ and $G_2^{(1)}$
summary: For each integer $l\ge1$, we give closed formulas for the local energies on tensor squares of the level-$l$ perfect crystals of types $D_4^{(3)}$ and $G_2^{(1)}$, normalized to vanish at the all-zero coordinate tensors. The $D_4^{(3)}$ energy is the maximum of three defects, equivalently of nine linear forms in parameters of classical highest-weight elements. Eliminating these parameters yields the maximum of nine piecewise-linear functions of the twelve input coordinates. Tensor-compatible similarity identifies the $G_2^{(1)}$ energy at level $l$ with one third of the pullback of the $D_4^{(3)}$ energy at level $3l$, yielding the same coordinate formula. The formula has no explicit level dependence, respects natural coordinate-set inclusions between levels, and allows direct evaluation without the combinatorial $R$-matrix or crystal-graph traversal.

title: Generalized parabolic Demazure modules and the N!/2-conjecture for two-row diagrams
summary: We study a family of generalized parabolic Demazure modules, i.e. of gl[x]-submodules of tensor products of integrable representations of the affine Lie algebra generated by tensor products of extremal vectors, and describe these modules by generators and relations. Realizing the Garsia--Haiman modules of two-row diagrams as fusion products of two local Weyl modules, we show that their y-graded components admit filtrations whose associated graded modules are isomorphic to tensor products of these generalized parabolic Demazure modules with the cohomology rings of Grassmannians. As a consequence, the Garsia-Haiman modules of two-row diagrams of a fixed size generate a distributive lattice, and the N!/2-conjecture holds for two-row diagrams.

title: Extensions at Nonzero p-Characters for Cartan-Type Lie Algebras
summary: For restricted simple Cartan-type Lie algebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p\ge5$, the reduced enveloping algebra at every nonzero $p$-character is a matrix algebra over a terminal symmetric corner, and this corner determines the extensions. Central-socle traces recover its radical and its simple factors, and the first radical layer determines the degree-one extensions. For the Witt algebra $W(1;1)$, at even height $2\le h\le p-3$, the unique simple module has self-extension dimension $\min\{p-h-2,h+2\}$. At height two in characteristic seven, we present the Yoneda algebra as an eight-dimensional symmetric algebra tensored with a polynomial algebra on three central degree-two classes. An equivariant Tate resolution and cocycle identities prove the presentation in all degrees.

title: Multiplicity one for a linear spherical pair and its unitary analogue
summary: We prove multiplicity one for a linear spherical pair associated with $\mathrm{GL}_4(F)\times\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ and its unitary similitude analogue associated with $\mathrm{GU}(2,2)(F)\times\mathrm{GU}(1,1)(F)$. Both results hold for all irreducible admissible representations over non-Archimedean local fields of characteristic zero. Generalized Harish-Chandra descent reduces the proofs to the analysis of closed orbits and their normal representations. The unitary proof combines reductions to the linear case with a rational classification of closed orbits and a separate analysis of the remaining normal representations. We also establish multiplicity one for unitary Shalika periods of $\mathrm{GU}(2,2)(F)$ with arbitrary irreducible admissible coefficients. A theta-period identity relates these periods to the unitary spherical pair. By varying the splitting character, we prove that every irreducible admissible representation of $\mathrm{GU}(2,2)(F)$ occurs as a quotient of a suitable big theta lift, allowing the multiplicity-one bound to pass to the Shalika periods. The linear argument also recovers Rallis's multiplicity-one theorem for twisted Jacquet modules of $\mathrm{GL}_4(F)$.

title: Planar Convexity of Isotropy Orbits via Cohomology and Common Zeros
summary: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a noncompact simple real Lie algebra with a Cartan decomposition $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{k}\oplus\mathfrak{p}$. Let $K$ denote the connected Lie group corresponding to $\mathfrak{k}$. Then $K$ acts on $\mathfrak{p}$ via the adjoint representation. In this paper, we prove that for every $C\in\mathfrak{p}$ and every real linear map $L:\mathfrak{p}\to\mathbb{R}^2$, the linear image $L(K\cdot C)$ of the orbit $K\cdot C\subset\mathfrak{p}$ is convex in $\mathbb{R}^2$, except for the circle orbits when $\mathfrak{g}\cong\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb{R})$ and $C\ne0$. By the two-piece property of isotropy orbits, any point omitted from the interior of the convex hull of a planar projection induces a nonzero class in the first integral cohomology of the orbit. This class vanishes directly in the non-Hermitian case, whereas in the Hermitian case we show that it vanishes by using the central circle action and a common-zero theorem of Gichev for Laplace eigenfunctions. Our approach treats classical and exceptional noncompact simple real Lie algebras uniformly and extends to real semisimple Lie algebras via Minkowski sums.

title: Calogero-Moser Polynomial Approximations and Dwork Congruences for Complete Flags
summary: We construct $p$-adic polynomial approximations to the zero-framing cohomological quasimap vertex of cotangent bundles to complete flag varieties from the trigonometric Calogero--Moser system. Negative integer couplings give regular staircase Jack polynomials with nonnegative integer coefficients. We compare them with complete-flag master polynomials extending the construction of Smirnov--Varchenko. Both families converge coefficientwise to the vertex and satisfy the full commuting equations modulo $p^s$. For $n\geq3$, we prove sharp degree-dependent congruences and compute leading residues at every $p$-power scale. Their discrepancy has coefficient norm $p^{-1}$ and an exact weighted Gauss norm giving uniform decay on smaller closed polydiscs. For the master family, multivariable Dwork congruences reconstruct the vertex by an infinite product. The results hold in every rank for $0<r/d\leq1/2$ and odd prime $p$.

title: Normality of closures of conormal bundles to Schubert cells for $\operatorname{GL}_n$
summary: We prove normality of closures of the conormal bundle to certain Schubert cells in the flag variety for $\operatorname{GL}_n$ coming from Grassmannians. Our argument uses a Zelevinsky-type resolution of singularities, and through a sequence of cohomological computations based on the Borel--Weil--Bott theorem, we reduce normality to a problem about Kronecker coefficients, which we solve by applying results of Knutson and Tao from honeycomb theory.

title: Koszul duality for boundary categories
summary: We study how Koszul duality relates two kinds of boundary constructions associated with a smooth category and a proper category. For a smooth category with a proper Koszul-dualizing subcategory, we construct a fully faithful functor from its categorical neighborhood of infinity to the singularity category associated to the proper category. We prove that this functor is an equivalence precisely when the smooth category is reflexive, meaning that it can be reconstructed from its finite-dimensional module theory. Under a Gorenstein condition, satisfied in the Calabi--Yau setting, the functor is induced by restriction of modules. We give algebraic criteria that ensure equivalence and obtain an identification of Hochschild cohomology.

title: Functoriality probes over number fields by mixed zero correlations
summary: We use an automorphic L-function over one number field as a probe for the functorial structure of another automorphic L-function over a possibly different field. No automorphic induction is assumed. We first determine the mixed Euler factors arising from the explicit formula, including the residue-degree multiplicities that occur when local traces are grouped by absolute norm. This local analysis gives four probe constructions. Rational-field probes with known base change detect constituent multiplicities and, in equal rank, exact Satake equalities. Probes over a common Galois field detect conjugacy and stabilizers. Dirichlet-character probes give congruence-weighted combinations of Satake traces even when the leading overlap vanishes. A tensor-product construction realizes general different-field probes whenever the required base changes exist. We then separate the pair calculation from the higher connected calculations and work out the cubic and quartic arithmetic explicitly. In an explicit small Fourier box these expressions yield all finite secondary orders of the centered statistics; the required pair prime number theorems also give raw and distinct-index correlations. The main analytic tools are an independent fixed-data proof of Hypothesis H over number fields, a positive-margin estimate for rationally grouped coefficients, and the theorem of Harcos-Thorner for the realized Rankin-Selberg factors. This expanded version includes the full computations, local examples, and an appendix explaining the character-extension issue avoided by the proof of Hypothesis H. The resulting probes give concrete tests of functorial relationships, while recovery of automorphic induction remains a longer-term goal.

title: Probing automorphic induction through zero correlations and secondary arithmetic terms
summary: Zero correlations offer a way to test the cuspidal structure of an automorphic L-function, but their leading self statistics retain only coarse degree and multiplicity data. We therefore adjoin a specified cuspidal L-function as a probe and study the resulting raw mixed correlations. Assuming a factorization into cuspidal L-functions over Q, we show that a mixed pair statistic detects the probe's occurrence and recovers its multiplicity. A suitable Gevrey-order-two test eliminates the smooth-density terms and gives a subexponential error. For arbitrary smooth plateau tests, the prime number theorem of Harcos and Thorner gives an error smaller than every fixed inverse power of log T, without a self-contragredience assumption. The stronger prime number theorem of Liu and Ye gives a subexponential remainder under its stated structural assumptions, with the possible norm-twist terms made explicit. To obtain arithmetic information beyond this overlap, we compute the correlation expansion at every fixed level and inverse-logarithmic order within the original strict small-support range. We treat the pair and higher correlations separately, using Jiang's rational-field fixed-data estimates to justify the required prime-power convergence. The pair calculation identifies the mixed arithmetic finite parts and gives detailed error estimates, including the contribution of norm twists. The higher-level calculation retains connected prime-power invariants, whose first cubic contribution appears at order (log T)^{-3}. Explicit third- and fourth-level formulas and examples explain the arithmetic content of these coefficients and the limitations of self-correlations. Varying powers of the probe separates their mixed components. These formulas, together with the distinct-index sieve, provide a collection of arithmetic probe responses toward the further problem of recovering automorphic induction structure.

title: A proof of the sharpness conjectures for all saturated fusion systems
comment: Lean and Rocq unconditional formalisations (about 62,000 and 100,000 lines of project source). Compilation on personal laptop took about 2.7 hours for Lean under Windows and 3.4 hours for Rocq under Linux. There is a report that describes the details of the formalisations and the underlying theories. See the acknowledgemets for more details
summary: We prove the Díaz$\unicode[Arial]{x2013}$Park conjecture for sharpness of saturated fusion systems. More generally, for every saturated fusion system $\mathcal F$ over a finite $p$-group and every Mackey functor for $\mathcal F$ over the localisation $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ of the integers at $p$, the higher limits of its contravariant part over the centric orbit category vanish in all positive degrees. In particular, the subgroup and normaliser decompositions of every $p$-local finite group $(S,\mathcal F,\mathcal L)$ over the $\mathcal F$-centric subgroups are sharp. This answers in the affirmative a question in the list of important open problems in [M. Aschbacher, R. Kessar and B. Oliver, Fusion Systems in Algebra and Topology, Cambridge Univ. Press (2011)], and proves the sharpness conjecture stated in [M. Aschbacher and B. Oliver, Fusion systems, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (2016)] and Conjecture 1.2 of [E. Yalç$\unicode[Arial]{x131}$n, Higher limits over the fusion orbit category, Adv. Math. (2022)]. The proof is algebraic and does not rely on the classification of finite simple groups.

title: RaFH and CRaFH superalgebras: Frobenius forms, representation theory and respectability
summary:
We introduce \emph{RaFH superalgebras}, which are Rees affine Frobenius Hecke superalgebras. These algebras are defined by generators and relations, using \emph{Frobenius-tensor superalgebras} to axiomatise tensor powers of Frobenius superalgebras together with their copairing elements. The RaFH superalgebras include, as special cases, the affine and degenerate affine Hecke algebras of type $A$, the affine Sergeev superalgebras, the affine wreath product algebras and quantum affine wreath algebras, as well as the recently introduced quantum wreath product algebras in the special case of the superflip braiding. We study the RaFH superalgebras from both structural and representation theoretic points of view. We prove a basis theorem for the RaFH superalgebras, construct universal Jucys--Murphy elements, and classify their simple modules over an algebraically closed field via atomic superalgebras, which are smaller RaFH superalgebras of Hecke, Clifford or wreath type.
  We then study \emph{CRaFH superalgebras}, which are the cyclotomic quotients of the RaFH superalgebras. We construct bases for these superalgebras, and compute the Gram determinants of natural trace forms, and use these to determine when these superalgebras are symmetric or Frobenius. To study the representation theory of the CRaFH superalgebras, we introduce the \emph{respectable algebras}, which is a vast generalisation of cellular algebras, standardly based algebras and finite dimensional affine cellular algebras, and give many examples illustrating their variety and ubiquity. We then show that CRaFH superalgebras are respectable algebras with weight poset given by multipartitions that are coloured by the representations of the underlying Frobenius algebra. This result can be viewed as a far-reaching generalisation of Murphy's bases into the setting of CRaFH algebras.

title: Siegel-Weil type identities for general linear groups related to parabolic induction from two Speh representations
summary: We prove identities of Siegel-Weil type for Eisenstein series on general linear groups, attached to parabolic induction from two Speh representations corresponding to the same irreducible, cuspidal representation. Such an identity relates a residue, at a (simple) pole of an Eisenstein series, as above, to a value of a similarly structured Eisenstein series at a point of holomorphy.

title: A faithful representation and profinite completion
summary: We exhibit two finitely generated residually finite groups $G_1$ and $G_2$ with isomorphic profinite completions $\widehat{G_1} \cong \widehat{G_2}$, such that $G_1$ has a faithful representation into $GL(d,\mathbb{C})$ but $G_2$ is not linear. This answers a question of Andrei Jaikin-Zapirain, Alexander Lubotzky, and Martin Bridson negatively. We also present two finitely generated residually finite groups $H_1$ and $H_2$ with isomorphic profinite completions $\widehat{H_1} \cong \widehat{H_2}$ satisfying the following. For every field $k$ with characteristic $p \geq 5$ and transcendence degree $r \geq 2$, there exists $d>0$ such that $H_1$ has a faithful representation into $GL(d,k)$. However, $H_2$ admits no faithful finite-dimensional representation over any field of positive characteristic.

title: The inductive Navarro-Alperin weight condition for the Suzuki and Ree groups
summary: In this paper, we give verifications of the inductive Navarro-Alperin weight condition in [8] for the Suzuki and Ree groups at all primes.

title: Idempotent Ultrafilters and Closed Images of Complete Semilattices
summary: We prove that every continuous homomorphism from a complete topologized semilattice to a Hausdorff semitopological semilattice has closed image, answering a question of Banakh and Bardyla. The main step is the convergence of idempotent ultrafilters on complete semitopological semilattices. We also prove that, for every complete subsemilattice $X$ of a Hausdorff semitopological semilattice $Y$, the natural order of $X$ is closed in $Y\times Y$. In particular, the natural order of every complete Hausdorff semitopological semilattice $X$ is closed in $X\times X$.

title: The most singular loci of twisted character varieties
summary: For any simply connected almost simple group $G$ and any compact Riemann surface of genus $g>1$, we study the singular locus of the character variety which parametrises fundamental group representations with a twist by a central element $z$ of $G$. While for $z=1$ the most singular representations have values in a maximal torus (and are invariant for the Weyl group action) and for generic $z$ every $z$-twisted representation is irreducible, for a general $z$ we find that the most singular representations have values in a particular Levi subgroup $L_z$ up to conjugation. From the explicit Lie-theoretic description of $L_z$, we determine the structure of the maximal stabiliser groups, and prove that the most singular loci is a disjoint union of generic type $A$ character varieties.

title: Whittaker modules for the principal $W$-algebra $\mathcal W^k(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$ via free field realizations
summary: We study Whittaker and generalized Whittaker modules for the universal principal $W$-algebra $\mathcal W^k(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$, using two free field realizations: one in the Heisenberg vertex algebra of rank two and the other in the tensor product of the universal Virasoro vertex algebra with the Heisenberg vertex algebra of rank one. Under explicit conditions on the parameters, we construct universal Whittaker modules, establish their ordered bases, and obtain explicit irreducibility criteria. Under an explicit nondegeneracy condition, we also show that the submodules of these tensor products correspond to the submodules of the Virasoro factor. We prove irreducibility of the universal Whittaker modules constructed in this paper.

title: The Yangian associated with the binary tree
summary: In this article, we give three candidates for a definition of the Yangian associated with the binary tree $X^*$ and the group $Aut(X^*)$ consisting of automorphisms of $X^*$ which preserve the tree structure. The first candidate has the Schur-Weyl duality with one kind of an extension of the degenerate affine Hecke algebra. The second and third ones have a homomorphism corresponding to the wreath recursion.

title: Categorifications of noncrossing partitions of type B and affine type A
summary: The lattice of wide subcategories of a tube is isomorphic to the lattice of noncrossing partitions of type B. We prove that through this categorification of noncrossing partitions, Kreweras complement is taking left perpendicular categories. With the help of this categorification and weighted projective lines, we obtain an inclusion from the lattice of noncrossing partitions of type B_n to a lattice of affine type A_n which preserves Kreweras complement.

title: Auslander-type grade conditions and subcategories related to syzygy modules
summary: The question of when a syzygy module or a module satisfying a Serre condition satisfies the cohomological vanishing conditions known as higher torsionfreeness has been extensively studied. In this paper, we address these questions using grade conditions introduced and studied by Auslander-Bridger and Auslander-Reiten. We also investigate homological conditions on Ext modules and, as an application, give a partial answer over commutative rings to a question of Auslander-Bridger concerning whether higher reflexive modules are higher torsionfree.

title: $AV$-modules on affine algebraic groups
summary: We study $AV$-modules on an affine algebraic group $G$, that is, modules that admit compatible actions of the algebra of regular functions on $G$ and the Lie algebra of vector fields. A central role in this theory is played by the Lie algebra of jets of vector fields. Our main result is the Decomposition Theorem for the Lie algebra of jets of vector fields. We apply the Decomposition Theorem to describe differentiable $AV$-modules on $G$.

title: Relative Rouquier linearity and inverse hybrid Kazhdan-Lusztig positivity
summary: We prove signed positivity for the expansion of a parabolic hybrid basis in the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis of a Hecke algebra. The coefficients have degree bounded by the length of the corresponding minimal coset representative. We deduce this linearity from Elias-Williamson's ordinary Rouquier linearity by a truncation argument. The result does not require the parabolic subgroup to be finite.

title: A proof of the Zariski closure conjecture and quasi-Frobenius exponential algebras
summary: Let $G=\exp(\g)$ be an exponential solvable Lie group, $π\in\widehat G$, and $Ω_π$ the coadjoint orbit attached to $π$ by the orbit method. The Zariski closure conjecture asserts that the Poisson characteristic variety $\VA(π_ν)$ of the deformed representation coincides with the Zariski closure of $Ω_π$ in $\g^*$. Known until now only in special situations, including the nilpotent case, it is proved here in full generality. Since the Hilbert space of $π$ is a quantization of the symplectic manifold $Ω_π$, the statement says that the passage back from the representation to the orbit, a dequantization, loses nothing: the orbit is recovered, up to Zariski closure, from the algebra alone. We also characterize the quasi-Frobenius exponential Lie algebras, those whose dual vector space is a Zariski-dense coadjoint orbit, through the triviality of the annihilator of an irreducible representation.

title: Spherical Schubert varieties in $GL_n / P$
summary: Let a general linear group act on a partial flag variety transitively, and consider the induced action of a Levi subgroup $L$. A Schubert variety is $\textit{$L$-spherical}$ if it is stable under the $L$-action and contains a dense open orbit of a Borel subgroup of $L$. It is $\textit{toric}$ if, in addition, $L$ is a torus. In this paper, we give a combinatorial classification of $L$-spherical Schubert varieties in partial flag varieties. This is achieved by applying Lakshmibai-Seshadri paths forming crystal graphs of Demazure modules. Previously, Hodges and Lakshmibai classified $L$-spherical Schubert varieties in Grassmannians. $L$-spherical Schubert varieties in complete flag varieties were treated independently by Gao-Hodges-Yong and Can-Saha. Our classification generalizes and unifies these results.

title: Distortion of Random Max Filters over Reflection Groups
summary:
A max filter with Gaussian templates $a_1,\dots,a_D$ is a
  $G$-invariant map $\R^d\to\R^D$, where $G$ is a finite reflection group. As
  $D\to\infty$ its distortion converges a.s to the condition number of
  $M_G^{1/2}$, where $M_G$ is the second-moment matrix of a standard Gaussian
  vector moved into a fundamental chamber of $G$. We compute this limit exactly
  for the sign and dihedral groups, and show it grows as $Θ(\sqrt d)$,
  $Θ(d^{3/2})$ and $Θ(k)$ for the sign, symmetric and dihedral groups of order $2k$. The
  symmetric case bound uses a lower bound on the covariance of order
  statistics. For any finite $G$ we also show that the infimum defining the optimal lower Lipschitz
  constant of a piecewise-linear $G$-invariant map is a minimum.

title: Cuspidal sheaves on the stack of L-parameters
summary: We introduce the notion of cuspidal coherent sheaves on the moduli stack of local L-parameters. We give a complete classification and relate them to Lusztig's cuspidal local systems (or character sheaves). Under the categorical local Langlands conjecture, these sheaves are expected to correspond to supercuspidal representations supported at basic points. We also construct semiorthogonal decompositions of the category of coherent sheaves on the moduli stack of L-parameters that conjecturally match the semiorthogonal decompositions of sheaves on $\mathrm{Bun}_G$ coming from the stratification by the Kottwitz set and Bernstein decomposition of representation categories.

title: Haiman's conjecture for n <= 10: Kazhdan-Lusztig positivity of monomial immanants
comment: 25 pages. Companion to arXiv:2610.39021. Code: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23730750; data: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23532289. v2: credits Haiman 1993 for the inclusion C_KL in C_J and the values at w_0(mu); results and numbering unchanged
summary:
Haiman conjectured that for every partition $λ\vdash n$ and every $w\in S_n$ the polynomial $c_{λ,w}(q)$, a monomial character of the Hecke algebra evaluated at the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis, has non-negative integer coefficients and is symmetric and unimodal, and he verified this by computer for $n\le7$. We verify it for every $n\le10$. A stability lemma reduces the statement to $n=10$, which we settle by an exact computation that stores only the 1,252,173,030 pairs $(x,w)$ in $S_{10}$ with $x$ maximal in its double coset for the descent sets of $w$, and takes the traces of the standard basis from the class polynomials of Geck and Pfeiffer. Every stored Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial agrees with du Cloux's Coxeter3, and the coefficients pass several independent checks, including a comparison at all 16,796 codominant $w$ with chromatic quasisymmetric functions computed from colourings.
  Consequently, for $n\le10$ every monomial immanant is a non-negative integer combination of Kazhdan-Lusztig immanants, Stembridge's monomial immanant conjecture holds, and a class-function immanant is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices if and only if it is non-negative at the block matrices $J_μ$. We use this to describe the order of normalised irreducible-character immanants on totally non-negative matrices for $n\le10$, and to prove Pate's inequalities there. On the full span of permutation monomials we give a Newton-polytope criterion for the coefficient of $\mathrm{Imm}_w$ to be non-negative throughout the totally non-negative cone, show that for $n=4,5$ this happens exactly when $X_w$ is smooth, and check by exact computation for $n\le10$ the proof of this for all $n$ given in a companion paper.

title: Hook monomial immanants are Kazhdan-Lusztig positive
comment: 26 pages, 7 figures, 1 table. Companion to arXiv:2610.41555. Code and data: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23730750. v2: adds Corollary 5.2 (Murnaghan-Nakayama inequalities), a remark on the dual e-positive picture and a remark that proofs for new shapes must leave class functions; credits Haiman 1993 for the inclusion C_KL in C_J; other numbering unchanged
summary:
Stembridge conjectured that every monomial immanant is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices, and Haiman proposed a stronger statement which at $q=1$ says that every monomial immanant is a non-negative integer combination of the Kazhdan-Lusztig immanants of Rhoades and Skandera. We prove this for every hook shape $(a,1^{n-a})$ and every $n$. More precisely, each of the per-vertex functions obtained by splitting Stembridge's formula for hook characters is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive.
  The main tool is a positivity statement for products: a product of Kazhdan-Lusztig positive immanants of complementary submatrices is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive, which we deduce at $q=1$ from Braden's hyperbolic localization, following Billey and Braden. With Haiman's theorem for irreducible characters, it shows that every class function whose Frobenius characteristic lies in the semiring generated by Schur functions and hook monomial symmetric functions is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive; for example, Skandera's chain of normalised hook immanants is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive for every $n$.
  We place these results in a comparison of three cones of class functions, and show that the remaining obstructions to Haiman's conjecture lie at singular Schubert varieties that are not reached by an iterated doubling identity of Abreu and Nigro, for which we give an explicit criterion. Finally, on the full span of permutation monomials, an element that is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices can have a negative coefficient at the Kazhdan-Lusztig immanant $\mathrm{Imm}_w$ if and only if the Schubert variety $X_w$ is singular; Skandera proved the smooth half.

title: Infinite Girth, Finite Quotients, and Nielsen Connectivity in Groups
comment: Many new results were added to the current version (e.g. Theorem A, Corollary B & Corollary C), and many structural changes were made. The Question 1.1 is completely resolved now. Question 1.2 was added and also resolved. Section 5.3, 6.1, and 6.2 are added to the last question and remark section
summary:
We develop new methods for studying infinite girth in finitely generated residually finite groups, particularly those containing no non-abelian free subgroups and satisfying no non-trivial group law. Our main contribution is a probabilistic Nielsen-component lifting principle, based on product replacement graphs, which provides a criterion for transferring suitable generation and word-avoidance properties of finite quotients to the ambient group.
  As an application, we prove that every finitely generated group admitting infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic non-abelian finite simple quotients has infinite girth, with extensions to quasisimple and, under additional hypotheses, almost-simple quotients. We further establish infinite girth for the B. H. Neumann group and the Bou-Rabee-Seward group, obtaining new results on the occurrence of non-abelian finite simple quotients and sections. By a different construction, we also prove that Alt_fin(Z) semidirect Z has infinite girth. Finally, we establish a marked finite-quotient characterization of infinite girth for finitely generated residually finite groups and prove that, for linear groups over fields of characteristic zero, large marked girth can be realized in congruence quotients. We conclude with several open questions and remarks arising from our results.

title: Iwahori Gaiotto conjecture for cotangent type
summary: We study the Iwahori Gaiotto conjecture for cotangent types and its application to the representation theory of the (mixed, small, and Lusztig) quantum supergroups. Using local and global models and SW-Zastava spaces, we construct factorization functors and compare the Iwahori Gaiotto category with the category $O$ of the mixed quantum supergroup. We then study the images of intersection cohomology sheaves and the metaplectic Hecke action. In type A, we describe the finite and affine monodromic categories, the corresponding Yokonuma--Hecke actions, and their role in the Kazhdan--Lusztig algorithm. The last section treats the pointwise purity.

title: Equivariant Cleft Extensions and Singular Equivalences
comment: 16 pages. v2: Corrections and additions. Comments are welcome!
summary: We study the equivariant lifting of cleft extensions of abelian categories and its impact on singularity categories. Specifically, we establish the necessary framework for lifting a cleft extension to a G-equivariant cleft extension. Furthermore, we prove that a restriction functor associated to a cleft extension induces a singular equivalence if and only if its equivariant counterpart does. As a concrete application, we demonstrate that the skew group ring of a $G$-equivariant $θ$-extension is isomorphic to a $\widehatθ$-extension of the base skew group ring, allowing us to lift singular equivalences for these structures.

title: Orthosymplectic Quantum Groups Revisited
summary: We present the RLL-realization of extended orthosymplectic quantum supergroups for any parity sequence, with R-matrices evaluated in the earlier work [Lett. Math. Phys. 116 (2026), 55, 97 pages, arXiv:2408.16720]. Our isomorphism is compatible with the internal structure of generalized doubles. We also relate different sign conventions through 2-cocycle twists.

title: A Non-graded Koszul Duality and Its Applications
summary: Let \(Λ\) be a finite-dimensional Koszul algebra with Koszul dual \(Λ^!\). We establish derived Koszul dualities at the level of bounded derived categories, both in the graded setting \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(Λ\textup{-gmod})\) and in the ungraded setting \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(Λ\textup{-mod})\), without imposing finiteness conditions on \(Λ^!\). We first prove a graded derived Koszul duality for every finite-dimensional Koszul algebra, with no Noetherian or coherence assumptions on the Koszul dual. We then show that the bounded derived category \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(Λ\textup{-mod})\) can be reconstructed from the graded theory as the triangulated hull of an orbit category. This yields a genuinely non-graded derived Koszul duality. We further establish singular and dg refinements of these dualities. For Iwanaga--Gorenstein Koszul algebras, this gives a stable Koszul duality for graded Gorenstein-projective modules and their ungraded counterparts, providing a non-graded form of the Bernstein--Gel'fand--Gel'fand correspondence. As applications, we obtain new descriptions of the bounded derived categories \(\mathsf{D}^{b}(\mathcal{O}_λ)\) for all integral blocks of category \(\mathcal{O}\), including singular blocks, thereby closing a gap left open in the work of Beilinson, Ginzburg, and Soergel. We also establish analogous dualities for certain categories of perverse sheaves arising in geometric representation theory. Finally, we formulate conjectural descriptions of bounded derived and singularity categories of finite-dimensional graded algebras in terms of dg orbit categories.

title: iCanonical basis arising from quasi-split rank one iquantum group
comment: v2: 43 pages, major revision, formulated uniform transition formulas between monomial and icanonical bases including previously separate boundary cases b=a+c (the old boundary case formulas were incorrect due to sign error in results in the literature); full transition formula from icanonical to canonical bases
summary: We compute icanonical basis of the quasi-split rank one modified iquantum group, by obtaining explicit transition matrices among the icanonical basis, monomial basis, and standardized canonical basis; all these bases can be naturally categorified. These transition matrices follow from their counterparts computed in this paper among the icanonical basis, monomial basis, and canonical basis on simple finite-dimensional modules of quantum $\mathfrak{sl}_3$.

title: A note on toric periods in unramified families
comment: Revised version, to appear in Proc. Indian Acad. Sci. (Math. Sci.)
summary: Let $A$ be the algebra $\mathbf{C}[X_1^{\pm 1},X_2^{\pm 1}]$ and $Q(A)$ its quotient field. In this short article we exhibit the correct normalization for the toric period on the parabolically induced unramified family over $Q(A)$, so that it behaves optimally under restriction to the parabolically induced unramified family over $A$. Finally, we explicitly describe the structure of the $A$-module given by the image of this normalized period. These results answer questions raised by D. Prasad, and point towards potential generalizations to a broader unramified Gan-Gross-Prasad setting.

title: The Derived Auslander--Iyama Correspondence II: Bimodule Calabi--Yau Structures
comment: 103 pages. v2: Corrected several small typos. Added new Section 7.3 on a non-enhanceable triangulated Calabi--Yau structure. v3: Editorial improvements. v4: Enhanced exposition, several small corrections. Subsection 7.3 is now Section 8. v5: Corrected Example 7.14, other minor edits
summary: Let $d$ be a positive integer. In a previous article we established a bijective correspondence between the following classes of objects, considered up to the appropriate notion of equivalence: differential graded algebras (dg) with finite-dimensional $0$-th cohomology such that the canonical generator of their perfect derived category is a basic $d\ZZ$-cluster tilting object, and basic Frobenius algebras that are twisted $(d+2)$-periodic as bimodules. In this article, we prove a variant of our general correspondence for bimodule right Calabi--Yau dg algebras. A novel ingredient is a new cohomology theory which contains obstructions to the existence and uniqueness of minimal $A_\infty$-bimodule structures on a graded bimodule. As an application of our results, we obtain, to our knowledge, the first example of an algebraic triangulated category with a triangulated Calabi--Yau structure that cannot be lifted to a bimodule right Calabi--Yau structure on any of its dg enhancements.

title: Search for a basis of the Temperley-Lieb algebra, using rewriting systems
comment: 35 pages. This document is an internship report from a bachelor student. It shows a lot of "known" results, except for part 2.1.2, giving the Jones normal form of a diagram; part 2.2.2-3, applying rewriting theory to find the Jones normal forms basis of the Temperley-Lieb algebra; and 4.3-4, applying category theory to find a new basis
summary: We begin by defining Temperley-Lieb algebra, in two different ways: as a presented algebra or as a diagrammatic algebra. Next, we look for a basis algorithmically, using rewriting theory. Finally, we introduce a generalization of the Temperley-Lieb algebra, which is an oriented version of the previous one. This pushes us to employ a more efficient tool, category theory, to use rewriting to easily obtain a basis for the algebra.

title: Partial character tables for $\mathbb{Z}_\ell$-spetses
summary:
Let ${\mathbb{G}}$ be a simply connected ${\mathbb{Z}}_\ell$-spets, let $q$ be a prime power, prime to $\ell$ and let $S$ be the underlying Sylow $\ell$-subgroup. Firstly, motivated by known formulae for values of Deligne-Lusztig characters of finite reductive groups, we propose a formula for the values of the unipotent characters of ${\mathbb{G}}(q)$ on the elements of $S$. Using this, we explicitly list the unipotent character values of the ${\mathbb{Z}}_2$-spets $G_{24}(q)$ related to the Benson-Solomon fusion system Sol$(q)$, and the Aguadé ${\mathbb{Z}}_5$-spets $G_{29}(q)$.
  Secondly, when $\ell > 2$ is a very good prime for ${\mathbb{G}}$, the Weyl group $W$ of ${\mathbb{G}}$ has order coprime with $\ell$, and $q\equiv1\pmod\ell$ we introduce a formula for the values of characters in the principal block of ${\mathbb{G}}(q)$ which extends the Curtis-Schewe type formulae for groups of Lie type, and which we show to satisfy a version of block orthogonality.
  In both cases we formulate and provide evidence for several conjectures concerning the proposed values.

title: Orbit structures on real double flag varieties for the Siegel parabolic subgroups
summary:
Let $ G $ be a connected reductive algebraic group over $ \mathbb{R} $, and $ H $ its symmetric subgroup. For parabolic subgroups $ P_{G} \subset G $ and $ P_{H} \subset H $, the product of flag varieties $ \mathfrak{X} = H/P_H \times G/P_G $ is called a double flag variety, on which $ H $ acts diagonally.
  Now let $G$ be either $\mathrm{U}(n,n)$ or $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}(\mathbb{R})$. We classify the $H$-orbits on $ \mathfrak{X} $ in both cases and show that they admit exactly the same parametrization. Concretely, each orbit corresponds to a signed partial involution, which can be encoded by simple combinatorial graphs. The orbit structure reduces to several families of smaller flag varieties, and we find an intimate relation of the orbit decomposition to Matsuki duality and Matsuki-Oshima's notion of clans.
  We also compute the Galois cohomology of each orbit, which exhibits another classification of the orbits by explicit matrix representatives.

title: Categorification of $k$-Schur functions and refined Macdonald positivity
comment: 69 pages. In v3, the full claim on the k-Schur positivity of Macdonald polynomials was withdrawn due to an error in Section 8 of v2; weaker/restricted results were recorded instead. In v4, corrected the treatment of the $\mathfrak g[z]$-action in Section 5 of v3 and made corresponding revisions. The main statements are unchanged from v3. Other minor corrections
summary:
We establish a substantial part of the categorification framework for $k$-Schur functions proposed in Chen's Ph.D.\ thesis, written under the supervision of Mark Haiman. More precisely, we realize $k$-Schur functions as the graded characters of a distinguished family of objects in a certain module category and establish module-theoretic analogues of several foundational properties of $k$-Schur functions. A final part of Chen's framework predicts a homological characterization of modules admitting filtrations by these distinguished objects; we establish this characterization under an additional combinatorial hypothesis.
  In addition, we unconditionally prove that modules arising in this framework admit filtrations whose subquotients are affine Demazure modules of level $k$. As a consequence, modified Macdonald polynomials expand positively in the characters of affine Demazure modules. This may be viewed as a homological refinement of Macdonald positivity, arising from an intrinsic $\mathrm{ext}$-orthogonality condition on the corresponding Garsia--Haiman modules. We also prove the combinatorial hypothesis for $m \le 2k$ in the appendix and verify it computationally for $m\leq 19$, yielding $k$-Schur positivity of modified Macdonald polynomials in these cases.
  Our approach builds on our previous work on the algebraic and geometric realization of Catalan symmetric functions, a class encompassing both $k$-Schur and Hall--Littlewood functions.

title: Building blocks for $W$-algebras of classical types
comment: Minor corrections and improvements, references updated, final version to appear in Forum of Math Sigma
summary: The universal $2$-parameter vertex algebra $W_{\infty}$ of type $W(2,3,4,\dots)$ serves as a classifying object for vertex algebras of type $W(2,3,\dots,N)$ for some $N$ in the sense that under mild hypothesis, all such vertex algebras arise as quotients of $W_{\infty}$. There is an $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$ family of such $1$-parameter vertex algebras which, after tensoring with a Heisenberg algebra, are known as $Y$-algebras. They were introduced by Gaiotto and Rapčák and are expected to be the building blocks for all $W$-algebras in type $A$, i.e., every $W$-(super) algebra in type $A$ is an extension of a tensor product of finitely many $Y$-algebras. Similarly, the orthosymplectic $Y$-algebras are $1$-parameter quotients of a universal $2$-parameter vertex algebra $W^{\text{ev}}_{\infty}$ of type $W(2,4,6,\dots)$, which is a classifying object for vertex algebras of type $W(2,4,\dots, 2N)$ for some $N$. Unlike type $A$, these algebras are not all the building blocks for $W$-algebras of types $B$, $C$, and $D$. In this paper, we construct a new universal $2$-parameter vertex algebra of type $W(1^3, 2, 3^3, 4, 5^3,6,\dots)$ which we denote by $W^{\mathfrak{sp}_2}_{\infty}$ since it contains a copy of the affine vertex algebra $V^k(\mathfrak{sp}_2)$. We identify $8$ infinite families of $1$-parameter quotients of $W^{\mathfrak{sp}_2}_{\infty}$ which are analogues of the $Y$-algebras. We regard $W^{\mathfrak{sp}_2}_{\infty}$ as a fundamental object on equal footing with $W_{\infty}$ and $W^{\text{ev}}_{\infty}$, and we give some heuristic reasons for why we expect the $1$-parameter quotients of these three objects to be the building blocks for all $W$-algebras of classical types. Finally, we prove that $W^{\mathfrak{sp}_2}_{\infty}$ has many quotients which are strongly rational. This yields new examples of strongly rational $W$-superalgebras.

title: Interval Replacements of Persistence Modules
comment: 76 pages. Accepted for publication in Discrete & Computational Geometry
summary: Persistence modules indexed by finite posets arise in topological data analysis. Unlike in the one-parameter case, they need not decompose into interval modules. Interval replacements approximate them by formal differences of interval decomposable modules. Extending earlier work on 2D-grids, we study these replacements for arbitrary compression systems. Different choices can give different interval rank invariants and replacements, including those related to interval resolutions on commutative ladders. Our main results are an explicit formula for interval ranks and an essential-cover theorem. Using Auslander--Reiten theory, we express interval ranks in terms of ranks of matrices formed from the structure maps of the module. The essential-cover theorem recovers each interval rank from a suitable restriction of the module. The replacement construction preserves the corresponding interval rank invariant, which recovers the usual rank invariant on segments. Essential covers also give a sufficient condition for two compression systems to yield the same invariant. For total compression, the invariant coincides with the generalized rank invariant of Kim and Mémoli. On 2D-grids, essential covers recover the zigzag formula of Dey, Kim, and Mémoli for this invariant.
